What is Nyxtok and what is it like to use?

Long image

A

Answer

Nyxtok is a self-hosted, TikTok-style feed of AI videos for one learner. Like a video, and Nyxtok transcribes it, fact-checks its claims on the web, and saves a Markdown note with an accuracy score.

  1. Every 6 hours a worker searches TikTok AI hashtags and keeps only viral, AI-relevant videos.1
  2. A like starts the pipeline: transcript, claim extraction, web research, classification and a summary.2
  3. The result is an Obsidian-style note in the vault folder, plus badges on the video card.3
  4. It is working code: four services that run with Docker Compose or on Railway.4

Applies toRepo NoJuanNobody/nyxtok at commit 208636cscreenshots are the real web UI run locally against a mock API with labelled example data

1

What happens, step by step?

Diagram structure
  • Hashtag search search
  • Viral + AI filters filter
  • Swipe the feed feed
  • Tap like like
  • Transcribe audio transcribe
  • Extract claims claims
  • Research and classify research
  • Vault note note
  • Card badges badge
  • claims → research · claims
  • feed → like
  • filter → feed · survivors
  • like → transcribe · enqueue
  • research → badge · score
  • research → note · report
  • search → filter · every 6 h
  • transcribe → claims · text
  1. Hashtag search ↗

    A cron worker searches 12 default AI hashtags, such as AI, LLM and ChatGPT.

  2. Viral + AI filters ↗

    A video stays if it has 100,000 views, or 10,000 likes with 5% engagement, and an AI score of at least 0.3.

  3. Swipe the feed ↗

    You see one full-screen video at a time, with Like, Save and Dismiss on the right.

  4. Tap like ↗

    Only a like starts the pipeline. Save and Dismiss just change the video's status.

  5. Transcribe audio ↗

    ffmpeg pulls the audio and Groq Whisper transcribes it; TikTok captions are the fallback.

  6. Extract claims ↗

    Groq llama-3.3-70b lists up to 30 factual claims from the transcript.

  7. Research and classify ↗

    Each claim is searched on DuckDuckGo, and up to 5 pages are read. The model labels it verified, partially verified, contradicted or unverifiable.

  8. Vault note ↗

    A Markdown note with transcript, claims, sources and score lands in the vault folder.

  9. Card badges ↗

    The card shows Transcribing, then Transcript and a "% verified" badge, with a toast.

2

What do you see in the app?

  • Feed: one full-screen video at a time, with Like, Save and Dismiss.
  • After a like: Transcribing… and Validating… badges; the card checks every 10 seconds.
  • Finished: a toast and a "% verified" badge.
  • Library: All, Liked, Bookmarked and Dismissed tabs, plus a Search page with a Watch later list.
3

What goes in, and what comes out?

ItemWhat it isWhere it lives
In: hashtagsTIKTOK_HASHTAGS, or 12 built-in AI tagsdiscovery worker
In: your tapsLike, Save, Dismiss, searchweb app → Fastify API
In: keysGROQ_API_KEY for Whisper and chat; AUTH_TOKEN for the APIenvironment variables
Out: feedFiltered AI videos with views, likes and hashtagsPostgreSQL videos table
Out: note{video_id}.md with frontmatter, transcript, claims, sourcesVAULT_PATH, default /data/vault
Out: scoreVerified claims ÷ all claims × 100DB column and note frontmatter

Videos you never like or save are deleted after 48 hours by default.5

api, discovery, web, Postgres
Users
One person; a single shared bearer token
Tests
31 of 32 Vitest tests passed in a local run

Gaps found in the code

The pipeline writes the score as 0–100, but the database column is DECIMAL(3,2) and the card multiplies by 100.7 This mismatch was not tested against a live database; scores may fail to save or show wrong. Notes are written to the server's disk; the web app shows only badges, not the note itself. The one failing test is "DB status updates correctly through the pipeline".
